stem: A 70-year-old woman has painful swallowing and burning behind the breastbone that began 3 weeks after she started a weekly tablet for osteoporosis. She takes it with a sip of water just before lying back down in bed. Endoscopy shows several erosions in the lower esophagus.
oneliner: 70F + new weekly tablet for osteoporosis + taken with a sip of water, then lies down + 3 wk later odynophagia + lower esophageal erosions → which drug?
ask: Which medication most likely caused this?

whyNot.A: **SERM**: risk is clots and hot flashes, not esophageal injury
whyNot.E: **Injection every 6 months**: no pill to stick in the esophagus

why: **Weekly osteoporosis tablet + little water + lying down → esophageal erosions** = pill esophagitis from a **bisphosphonate**. Take it upright with a full glass of water.

drug.name: Alendronate
drug.how: Binds bone hydroxyapatite and makes osteoclasts undergo apoptosis
drug.use: Osteoporosis, Paget disease, hypercalcemia of malignancy (IV forms)
drug.watch: Pill esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femur fractures
